_comment: Who fights whom. Slot geometry and per-slot label tuning are presentation and live in tools/build_battle.gd; this file only says which creature stands where. Format decided in design/encounters.md. An encounter is atomic — which encounter occurs, where, and in what world state is a region's question and deliberately not expressible here. A side may field one creature.

encounters.note: design/tutorial.md. Act one's duel: one creature each, so nothing about the Front/Back board has to be explained yet. Tidalpup is type-advantaged on purpose — Guard falls faster than HP only when you are, which is why capture is reachable here at all. The enemy is absent from the Charge economy (Tide resists Ember) and that is the point, not an oversight: a tutorial that can be lost is a tutorial the player fails before it teaches.
M3's proof battle, re-paired per design/first_blood_balance.md. Every correct target is diagonal, which is what forces the Front/Back reach rule into the fight.

The pre-repair roster. Kept because it is the counter-example every balance document cites: unwinnable by any explainable plan. It is deliberately not a valid encounter and excludes itself from sweeps by failing to discriminate.

design/second_encounter.md. Diagonal like first_blood, and mixed-type on purpose: a one-type enemy line cannot make a fight that rewards skill, because a creature whose attacks are all resisted never banks a Charge. Ashmoth is the visitor that wandered up from the kilns.
